message.reasoning:
I need to be careful with the design here. The regions include Switzerland and Germany, with Siemens trading on XETRA, but text-based KPIs can't score German or Swiss companies. The quant functions only cover US filers, so no quant source reaches every region except market factors, and those aren't theme exposure. I'll be upfront about that gap in the rationale, since Swiss and German names will show as unknown on text KPIs and rd_intensity is US-only too.

Sub-themes are grid_equipment_automation and energy_efficiency.

I'm weighing whether to include exclusions, but measuring them as exposure doesn't fit, so I'm leaning toward a single judgement gate on whether a company has any smart energy product or service at all, which would screen out pure fossil or EV-only names without hurting broad suppliers. I'm also settling the first KPI as smart energy revenue share, built from grid, automation, efficiency, demand response, storage and inverter revenue, with thresholds at 5%, 15%, 35% and 60%.

I'm setting the weights and thresholds for the next KPIs: a judgement score on grid automation offerings, a capex share for networks and storage with cutoffs from 10% to 65%, a judgement on efficiency and demand response, and storage/inverter revenue share starting at 2%. R&D intensity gets a 10-point weight as a US-only quant measure, and I'm tallying the running total toward a judgement gate on smart energy presence.

I'm going to make a judgement gate on whether a company has any smart energy product at all, since a revenue-share threshold would wrongly drop smaller second-tier suppliers. I'm also considering the revenue share KPI with lower thresholds, though disclosure might be patchy, so a presence judgement looks cleaner. Next I'm sorting the sub-themes into grid equipment and automation, efficiency and demand response, storage and inverters, and a digital innovation group.

I'm settling on five sub-themes now, with a core exposure group for the revenue-share and presence checks alongside grid equipment, efficiency and demand response, storage and inverters, and digital innovation. The plan is seven KPIs, with a revenue-share measure up front and a judgement gate on smart energy presence.

I'm settling the KPI list now: seven measures, with smart energy revenue share and a presence judgement up front, then grid automation, efficiency and demand response, storage and inverter revenue, and R&D intensity on the digital side, with weights summing to 100. I'll also keep the rubrics short and set the lookback at 550 days for filings and 450 for R&D.
